title: Unity Deck & Governance Signal
customer_attendees: Individual contributors and managers across Eng, Product, GX, Sales, Ops
summary: Company all-hands covering Q4 momentum update, a short governance/expenses signal, summary of the recent platform incident and remediation plan, product roadmap highlights for Private/Dedicated, and a temporary hiring pause. Leadership fielded questions about SLAs, pricing, and headcount. Clear next steps and owners assigned for incident doc, revised runbook, and hiring appeals.
topics: Platform incident postmortem and resiliency investments
Private deployment roadmap and compliance targets
Governance: expense approvals and procurement changes
transcript:
[00:00] Asha Patel: Morning everyone, thanks for being here. I know it's a big week. We'll run about an hour. Quick deck, a short governance announcement, then Q&A. We recorded this for folks who couldn't make it.

[00:37] Asha Patel: First — top line, Q4. We closed a couple of small deals late October, and usage on hosted API is up roughly 18% month over month. That's good. Gross margin is improving with batching and caching changes, but, uh, we still need to be disciplined on burn.

[01:15] Liam O'Connor: On throughput — we've seen median p95 latency creep on customer X workloads, partly due to increased long-context inferencing. Engineering has a plan to tune batching thresholds; we'll be rolling that in next two sprints.

[01:49] Maya Chen: For product, Private rollouts are on track for the compliance gating we promised; KMS integrations and the private control plane MVP will be in customer hands by late Jan. We still need a few more pieces for audit logs and retention policies.

[02:20] Diego Alvarez: Quick people note — we are going to institute a temporary hiring pause on non-critical IC roles. This is to extend runway while we lock the pricing changes. There will be a documented exception process. We'll share details on Monday.

[03:05] Audience: (murmurs)

[03:18] Asha Patel: I want to be clear — this isn't layoffs, it's pause-and-prioritize. We have committed hires for Dedicated support and platform stability teams; those continue. The ask is that managers hold off on new reqs unless they meet the exception criteria.

[04:05] Asha Patel: Now, on the incident — quick recap. Last Thursday we had an outage impacting hosted inference in us-west for about 40 minutes, elevated error rates for ~3 hours due to a combination of regression in kernel selection logic and a stale cache invalidation path.

[04:43] Liam O'Connor: The immediate fix was a rollback plus a hotpatch to the KV cache sweep. Root cause: an optimizer path that assumed stateless kernels for quantized variants. It was a chain — wrong kernel choice under a rare long-seq scenario which blew past our guardrails.

[05:10] Audience: [crosstalk] 'Was this the same thing as in staging?' 'No, it wasn't surfaced because our long-seq traffic pattern didn't hit test harness.'

[05:34] Maya Chen: We're putting stronger integration tests around sequence distribution and I've asked the infra team to add a synthetic long-context load to our preflight matrix. Also, the rollout checker will now require a fallback policy review.

[06:05] Sanjay Rao: Operationally, we need faster fallback triggers. We're implementing an automated model variant routing policy — if p95 passes threshold we'll degrade to a compatible lower-cost variant in that region. This is part of the resilience plan.

[06:47] Diego Alvarez: Communication postmortem will be centralized. For customers who were affected, CS already issued proactive notes; we'll follow up with a formal incident report and an offer to run a joint benchmark if they want.

[07:20] Asha Patel: Ok, moving to finance. We have to optimize unit economics. That means tightening default batching defaults, pushing customers toward recommended quantization profiles, and revising reserved capacity pricing. We'll balance that with a credits program for strategic accounts.

[07:56] Audience: 'Will this change our free tier?'

[08:05] Asha Patel: No immediate change to free trials. Pricing changes will target enterprise and dedicated contracts; we will communicate at least 60 days in advance for hosted customers. All billing changes go through the normal legal and finance channels.

[08:34] Maya Chen: Product roadmap — the big bets for next two quarters: 1) private control plane GA, 2) SDK 2.0 with structured outputs and better function calling ergonomics, 3) Optimize: an insights module to suggest per-route batching/quant settings. We're trimming experiments that don't hit product-market signals.

[09:10] Liam O'Connor: On Dedicated, we will offer two capacity classes: predictable and burstable. Predictable will have tighter SLAs and higher commit pricing; burstable will be cheaper but no SLA. We need sales to align offers to customer criticality.

[09:48] Sanjay Rao: Reliability investment — extra SRE headcount and budget for runbook automation. We're also putting a stronger emphasis on telemetry — token-level tracing to quickly identify kernel mismatches, which was a blind spot last week.

[10:20] Audience Question (Priya, Eng): Are we changing the release cadence?

[10:30] Liam O'Connor: Not fundamentally. We will add mandatory canary evaluation for kernel changes and long-seq synthetic checks. Rolling windows will be longer for risky kernel patches.

[11:05] Asha Patel: Governance changes next — short, but important. Effective immediately: expenses over $10k need a second sign-off from finance; vendor procurement for infra requires security approval; and any large cloud spend increase requires exec approval. These are to reduce blast radius.

[11:35] Diego Alvarez: We'll update the policies doc and run a short training for managers. Also, hiring exceptions should be routed to Diego + Asha with a 48-hour review SLA for business-critical asks.

[12:02] Audience: 'What about comp cycles and promotions?'

[12:10] Diego Alvarez: Comp cycle remains but we're deferring non-critical promotions until Q1 review; we'll honor previously committed promotion offers and make exceptions for performance-critical roles.

[12:45] Maya Chen: Community and OSS — we had good traction on the connector library. We'll open a new roadmap issue and plan to highlight two community contributions per month. This is part of our adoption channel.

[13:12] Audience Question (Tomas, Sales): How are we communicating pricing to high-touch accounts?

[13:20] Asha Patel: Sales and Solutions should coordinate: CSM to send a heads-up email and Solutions to run a quick usage optimization call. Finance will provide pre-approved credits for renegotiation.

[13:50] Liam O'Connor: Quick technical aside — for customers who must be low-latency and low-cost, our recommended pattern is: quantized LLM + local KV cache + smart batching. We'll publish a short best practices doc by end of next week.

[14:24] Audience: (applause)

[14:40] Asha Patel: Open Q&A now. Please keep it to two minutes per person so others can ask.

[15:00] Audience Question (Vivian, Eng): For the incident postmortem, will the timeline include the internal decision points?

[15:12] Maya Chen: Yes, it'll include timestamps, who signed off on the rollback, and the remediation steps. We'll redact any customer PII.

[15:45] Audience Question (Jared, SE): Will customers be given credits for the outage?

[15:53] Diego Alvarez: We're evaluating on a case-by-case basis. For proactive customers we offered a one-time credit; for strategic accounts we'll negotiate SLAs in their support contracts.

[16:20] Audience (Sasha, Product): Is the hiring pause going to affect the platform optimization team?

[16:30] Diego Alvarez: We're keeping platform optimization hires — those are high priority. Most recruiting pauses are for new headcount not directly tied to our resiliency or product roadmap commitments.

[17:00] Asha Patel: I want to highlight two wins: our embedding ingestion pipeline now handles 2x throughput with lower cost after the caching changes — shout out to the infra team — and our community connector had 3 external contributions this quarter.

[17:28] Audience: (cheering)

[17:45] Sanjay Rao: A couple of tactical asks from Eng leadership — please label any production experiment with a clear rollback plan and an owner. If you're doing kernel-level experiments, tag infra early.

[18:10] Audience Question (Nora, Marketing): Any change to external messaging about reliability?

[18:18] Asha Patel: We'll keep transparency but calibrated. Public postmortem and a summary blog are planned after we finalize the internal report. We won't call out customers.

[18:45] Audience: (multiple voices) 'Will there be a townhall specifically about the incident?'

[19:00] Asha Patel: No separate townhall — we'll put all details in the postmortem and make a short recorded walkthrough for anyone who wants deeper context.

[19:22] Liam O'Connor: Final technical note: kernel selection heuristics are getting a new feature flag that prevents the quantized path from taking precedence when sequence length > configured threshold. We'll default to safer behavior.

[20:00] Audience (Elena, Sales): Can we have a reusable slide deck for customer conversations about the incident and pricing changes?

[20:10] Maya Chen: Yes — comms + Product will produce a customer slide pack and a short FAQ for Sales and Solutions.

[20:35] Asha Patel: Closing notes — we are in a stronger position than many peers, but we need to be pragmatic. Expect tighter gating on spend, a small hiring pause, and a focus on stability. We'll revisit in the next all-hands.

[21:05] Asha Patel: Next steps — share the incident timeline doc by end of day Friday; share hiring pause policy Monday; product will publish the Private GA target and SDK 2.0 plan next week.

[21:30] Audience: (applause, meeting wraps)

[21:40] (Recording stops)
action_items: Maya Chen: Draft and publish incident timeline and postmortem by 2026-11-19
Liam O'Connor: Add long-sequence synthetic tests to preflight and enable canary for kernel changes (target: 2 sprints)
Diego Alvarez: Publish hiring pause policy and exception workflow by 2026-11-22
Product + Comms: Create customer slide pack and FAQ for incident/pricing changes by 2026-11-24
Sanjay Rao: Implement automatic model-variant fallback policy for p95 threshold within next quarter
next_steps: Incident postmortem and public summary (owners: Maya + Diego)
Hiring pause policy document and manager training (owner: Diego)
Best practices doc for low-latency / cost (owner: Liam)
Private control plane GA timeline confirmation (owner: Maya)
Revised dedicated capacity pricing proposal (owner: Finance)
